title: Autonomous KV policy steward: hit-rate digital twin, TTL surgicalizer, and safety-guard orchestration
creator: Priya Nair
description: Design and build an autonomous policy steward that recommends and safely applies KV/prefix cache configuration changes. The steward should produce TTL, bucket, and keying recommendations based on a hit-rate digital twin, quantify expected P50/P95 cost impact under workload mixes, and execute staged policy applies with automatic safety rollback. This ticket focuses on the modeling, simulation harness, and an opinionated safe-apply orchestration (shadow -> canary -> ramp -> full) integrated with current rollout tooling.
acceptance_criteria: Digital twin model produces per-prefix hit uplift / cost delta estimates with 90%+ calibration against holdout telemetry
Simulation harness can replay 30 days of production traces and produce deterministic rollout forecasts for candidate TTL changes
Safe-apply orchestration implements shadow, canary, and automated rollback triggers (hit_rate drop, token-cost spike, p95 latency increase)
Runbook and automated alerts created; SLO guardrails defined and tested in a dry-run environment
End-to-end demo run with one non-critical customer workload showing cost reduction without >2% increase in tail latency or >1% request failure rate
approach: Construct a modular pipeline: 1) hit-rate digital twin modeling request-to-prefix access patterns and cache dynamics; 2) TTL suggestion engine that reasons about batch-aware TTLs and key shaping; 3) simulation harness to estimate economics and risk; 4) orchestration layer that applies changes in shadow/canary/ramp stages and monitors guardrails for automated rollback. Recommendations include estimated hit uplift, cost change, and confidence bands.
modeling_methodology: Hybrid analytical + event-driven simulation. Steps: fingerprint prefix access distributions by tenant/route, fit per-prefix recency/frequency shapes (exponential/power-law mixtures), project hit-rate under candidate TTLs using closed-form approximations for LRU-like behavior, validate with Monte Carlo replay. Outputs: per-prefix expected hit_rate, delta cost/token, eviction rate, and variance estimates.
data_sources: production request logs (prefix labels, timestamps, route ids)
cache telemetry (inserts, evictions, hit/miss counters by prefix)
batching traces (batch sizes, queueing delay histograms)
billing telemetry (token counts, cost attribution by model/route)
simulation_plan: Deterministic replay pipeline consuming anonymized 30-day traces. Features: deterministic seeding, synthetic microburst injection, canonical cache semantics matching runtime configuration. Suites: baseline compare, randomized TTL perturbations, adversarial high-churn workload. Outputs: per-prefix/global cost and latency histograms and a risk score to rank candidates.
rollout_plan: Stages: shadow (48h collection), canary (1% traffic, 24-72h), ramp (10% traffic, 24-72h), full global apply with throttled ramp. Safety gates: automatic rollback on hit_rate drop, token-cost spike, or p95 latency regression. All stages produce comparison dashboards and prefix diff logs.
alerts_and_sla_guardrails: Hard alerts: per-tenant hit_rate delta < -10% sustained for 10 minutes or token_cost increase >15% for 5 minutes triggers immediate rollback. Soft alerts: predicted/actual divergence >20% for a prefix. Integrate with Slack and PagerDuty and create Console dashboard tiles for active steward runs.
rollback_playbook: Automated circuit-breaker revokes new policy and re-applies previous config, notifies owners, and marks rollout failed. Manual rollback via Console for partial restores. Fallback: isolate affected tenants by routing to a fallback model variant if automated rollback fails. Postmortem template auto-populated with traces, config diffs, and prediction vs actual comparisons.
notes_and_risks: Risks: model calibration drift on seasonal workloads; privacy constraints for per-tenant telemetry (require aggregation/anonymization); potential transient cost spikes during canary if traffic is not representative. Mitigations: require shadow validation with high confidence, throttled ramp, per-tenant isolation, and cross-team sign-off for enterprise tenants. Follow-on: extend steward to suggest batching config changes (max_batch_size, batch_timeout) and integrate with autoscaler heuristics.
